releases.title: Marty Stuart's Congress of Country Music Names Kim Vickers Executive Director
releases.body:
PHILADELPHIA, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Marty Stuart's Congress of Country Music has named Kim Vickers its new executive director, bringing more than three decades of experience in nonprofit leadership, fundraising and arts programming to the organization as it prepares for the anticipated 2027 grand opening of its country music museum in Philadelphia, Mississippi.

In her new role, Vickers will lead the Congress's operations, strategic planning, fundraising and community partnerships, working alongside founder Marty Stuart and the board of directors to advance the organization's mission of preserving and celebrating the history and cultural significance of country music through exhibits, education, and live performances.

"The Congress of Country Music began with a dream of creating a place where the stories, songs, and people who shaped country music would always have a home," said Marty Stuart, Grammy-winning Country Music Hall of Famer and founder of the Congress of Country Music. "As that dream continues to take shape, it takes the right people to help carry it forward. Kim brings the experience, heart, and leadership we need for this next chapter, and I'm proud to welcome her to the Congress family."

Vickers, a Certified Fund Raising Executive (CFRE), brings more than 30 years of experience advancing philanthropic initiatives, strengthening nonprofit organizations, and developing arts programming. Most recently, she served as director of development for the Mike Cottrell College of Business at the University of North Georgia, where she secured significant scholarship funding for students and increased the college's overall philanthropic support from the community, corporate partners, and alumni. Her career also includes development and leadership roles at Johns Hopkins University, the University of Maryland School of Medicine, and Agnes Scott College.

Beyond her experience in higher education, Vickers has a background in live entertainment and historic venue operations. From 2023 to 2025, she served as concert manager for The Holly Theatre in Dahlonega, Georgia, where she managed all aspects of its concert program, presenting 24 shows that raised funds in support of the community theater and its historic preservation efforts.

"Music and the arts have been at the heart of my life for as long as I can remember, and I've spent my career helping organizations build the support they need to do meaningful work," said Vickers. "This role brings those two passions together in a way I never imagined possible. To join the Congress just as the museum takes shape and the entire campus comes alive is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. I'm grateful to Marty and the board for their trust, and I can't wait to help share these stories with visitors from Philadelphia and around the world."

Vickers assumes leadership during a pivotal period for the Congress of Country Music as the organization builds on the success of its existing venues and prepares to expand its cultural and educational offerings.

Since reopening in 2022, the historic Ellis Theater has welcomed nationally recognized artists and audiences to downtown Philadelphia, establishing a growing presence for live entertainment in the community. The Congress has also completed the Cynthia Lake Building, providing administrative offices and artist accommodations, while construction progresses on the museum's Exhibit Hall.

Anticipated to open in 2027, the museum will showcase country music's rich history through artifacts and exhibits, including selections from the Marty Stuart Collection and additional artifacts presented in collaboration with the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum.

As executive director, Vickers will play a central role in bringing these elements together, strengthening the Congress's organizational infrastructure, expanding philanthropic and community support, and helping establish Philadelphia as a destination for country music history, education and entertainment.

About Marty Stuart's Congress of Country Music

Marty Stuart's Congress of Country Music is the spiritual home of country music, committed to touching lives by sharing experiences through exhibits, education and performances that inspire dreams for generations. The Congress aspires to touch lives through a real diversity of offerings in an authentic place unlike any other. Unique live performances, exhibits which honor both legends and newcomers and substantial educational offerings reach audiences across the state and country. Major performing artists are regularly featured alongside a solid season of events, integrated with revolving exhibits in collaboration with the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum. Our educational offerings will touch all ages and can be accredited and recognized for their influence.

releases.body:
From shelf to screen, the acquisition deepens Harvest Group's retail media expertise and expands its relationships with high-growth consumer brands

ROGERS, Ark., Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Harvest Group, a leading integrated commerce agency for high-growth consumer brands, today announced its acquisition of Good Peeps, a media agency specializing in retail advertising, digital campaign management and measurement. The move advances Harvest Group's goal of managing $10 billion in client retail sales and $2 billion in media spending.

As Harvest Group celebrates its 20th anniversary, the announcement is a continuation of its most significant transformation yet into the leading integrated commerce agency connecting retail strategy, media, data, and technology to accelerate brand growth. This year's strategic growth investments from Mountaingate Capital in March, followed by the acquisitions of Amazon-focused Cartograph in April and now Good Peeps, have all played a part in accelerating that transformation, expanding Harvest Group's capabilities, talent, and reach across the commerce ecosystem.

Founded in 2022 by Shray Joshi, Good Peeps has quickly established itself as a leading independent retail media agency, managing $100+ million in advertising spend. The agency has developed particular expertise across rapidly growing retail media platforms, including Instacart and DoorDash, Roundel, Walmart Connect and more, helping consumer brands translate advertising investments into measurable sales growth. 

"Retail is becoming increasingly complex, but data and technology are creating unprecedented opportunities to connect every aspect of commerce from discovery to purchase, across the physical and digital shelves of multiple retailers and digital platforms," said Ross Cully, founder and CEO of Harvest Group. "Scale isn't the goal; the goal is what scale makes possible for the high growth brands that we support. It creates powerful network effects through deeper retailer relationships, richer insights, and greater investments in talent and technology. Good Peeps accelerated that vision through the power of AI and good relationship building. Collectively, we believe that brands shouldn't have to choose between startup speed and innovation or the capabilities that come with scale. So, together, we're delivering both."

Harvest Group's existing clients will benefit from deepened expertise Good Peeps brings across the Instacart/DoorDash platform, as well as Good Peeps' AI-forward approach to media management. Good Peeps clients gain access to Harvest Group's broader connected service offering, including retail strategy, in-store and digital commerce, analytics, and social, all powered by the company's proprietary technology platform, along with its relationships at Walmart, Amazon, Target, Costco, Kroger and Sam's Club.

"I spent years on the brand side watching the digital shelf become some of the most important real estate in retail without getting the attention it deserved," said Shray Joshi, Founder of Good Peeps. "That's why we built Good Peeps. We teamed up with Harvest Group because they're the best at what they do and because of how they show up for people. Ross has spent 20 years building a company that takes care of its team and treats every client like they're the only one, and that's exactly the home the peeps deserve. Now it's one team helping brands win on the shelf and the screen."

Already supporting billions in annual client retail sales and managing hundreds of millions in media investments, Harvest Group is building toward an ambitious next chapter: $10 billion in client retail sales and $2 billion in media spend under management. By introducing the possibilities to Good Peeps' roster of CPG brands, Harvest Group plans to become the go-to agency for Founders and C-suites ready to generate long-lasting success on every shelf and every screen, for every CPG venture.

About Harvest Group

Founded in 2006, Harvest Group is an integrated commerce agency to high-growth consumer brands navigating today's complex retail landscape. The company offers integrated solutions that align strategy across in-store and digital commerce, retail media, and social platforms, all powered by the company's proprietary technology platform. With over 500 employees globally, Harvest Group works with brands at major retailers including Walmart, Sam's Club, Target, Amazon, Costco, and Kroger. For more information, visit www.harvestgroup.com.

DPR's family-focused benefits offer a model for supporting working parents in the construction industry

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- DPR Construction, a forward-thinking, self-performing builder, has been named to the 2026 Fortune Best Workplaces for Parents™ list, ranking No. 29 in the large-company category. This recognition highlights DPR's approach to supporting employees across different roles and stages of life, including those caring for children, parents and other family members.

The announcement comes during National Family Caregivers Month and underscores the importance of supporting working parents and caregivers across different roles and work environments. A 2026 Pew Research Center survey found that the difficulty of balancing work and family was nearly the same among parents who worked mostly from home and those who rarely or never did, 52% compared with 54%. For DPR, where employees work in offices, on jobsites and at facilities across the country, the findings reinforce the need to look beyond a single idea of caregiver support.

"Taking care of people has always been fundamental to who we are at DPR," said George Pfeffer, DPR Construction CEO and Leadership Team member. "People do their best work when they feel supported, included and connected. We focus on the whole person, from safety and wellbeing to belonging, career growth and life outside of work."

DPR offers a range of benefits designed to support employees (depending on tenure and union status) and their families, including:

  • Fertility, surrogacy and adoption assistance
  • Dependent-care spending accounts
  • Paid time off and leave, including pregnancy and parental leave
  • Parental coaching
  • Counseling and mental health resources for employees and their families

Additionally, DPR continues to add practical resources as employees' needs evolve and will roll out Helpr nationwide in 2027. Unlike traditional backup care, Helpr lets employees choose their own care, including paying the family, friends, and sitters they already rely on, so support reaches remote areas and covers hours outside the traditional daycare day. Employees can receive backup child care and elder care, plus guidance for longer-term needs like medical recovery, chronic illness and special-needs care.

The 2026 list was determined using survey responses from more than 650,000 employees with parenting responsibilities at Great Place To Work Certified™ companies, along with company data on benefits including parental leave, adoption, flexible scheduling, childcare and dependent health care. Companies were recognized based on the workplace experiences of working parents across job roles, work status and demographic groups.

The recognition builds on DPR's other workplace honors in 2026. DPR ranked No. 8 on the 2026 Fortune Best Workplaces in Construction™ list and was named to the 2026 PEOPLE® Companies that Care list. Earlier this year, 97% of DPR employees surveyed said the company is a great place to work.

releases.body:
INTERLOCHEN, Mich., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- This year in its centennial year, Interlochen Center for the Arts is proud to welcome 596 young artists from 47 states and 32 countries – including 47 creative writers, 52 dancers, 29 filmmakers and animators, 265 musicians, 124 thespians, as well as 53 visual and 26 interdisciplinary artists. Named by Niche as the #1 Best High School for the Arts in America for the second consecutive year, a central part of this award-winning education is their world-class faculty.

In its centennial year, Interlochen Center for the Arts is proud to welcome 14 new artistic and academic educators.

This academic year, Interlochen is thrilled to welcome 14 new artistic and academic educators to Interlochen Arts Academy, joining their existing, dedicated team of faculty, artists, and mentors. This new faculty will continue Interlochen's mission to create a singular place where young artists turn their passion and potential into purpose.

Recently announced is Interlochen's partnership with the Chicago Symphony, the Los Angeles Philharmonic, and the University of Michigan's University Musical Society (UMS) to mark Interlochen's centennial and promote world friendship with a March 2028 tour. Cristian Măcelaru and famed pianist Lang Lang—both celebrated international ambassadors for the arts—will be part this one-of-a-kind collaboration: Lang Lang will join students on Interlochen's campus for master classes and rehearsals and will perform with them on stage under the baton of Cristian Măcelaru for concerts at Interlochen's Corson Auditorium (March 10, 2028), Ann Arbor's Hill Auditorium at the University of Michigan (March 12, 2028), Chicago Symphony Center (March 14, 2028), and Los Angeles' Walt Disney Concert Hall (March 17, 2028).

Discover more about a few of Interlochen's new faculty members:

STEVE MYERSON, HAMANN FAMILY JAZZ PIANO CHAIR

Myerson's career has been shaped by celebrated jazz musicians and educators including Harold Mabern and Bill Charlap. Over the years, he has performed with diverse world-class artists including renowned bassist Christian McBride, legendary saxophonist Grover Washington Jr., and R&B group The Stylistics. He most recently served as Adjunct Professor of Jazz Studies at William Paterson University in New Jersey.

MICHAEL ROSSI, INSTRUCTOR OF VISUAL ARTS, SCULPTURE

Rossi is a professional metalworker with 25 years of experience and founder of Rossi Metal Design. In 2016, Rossi received the Grand Jury Award from the Preservation Alliance of Greater Philadelphia for the restoration of the two-story tall doors of Founder's Hall at Girard College. The following year, he was involved in the production and permanent installation of Grotto for Mona, a large-scale work by Randy Polumbo at the Museum of Old and New Art in Tasmania, Australia.

MICHAEL PIOTROWSKI, ADJUNCT INSTRUCTOR OF FILM & NEW MEDIA

Piotrowski is a veteran production sound mixer and member of the Cinema Audio Society. He has collaborated on major studio productions including Transformers, Star Trek, Ender's Game, and WandaVision. Piotrowski's work spans from large-scale action films to television, as well as independent productions. Originally from northern Michigan, Piotrowski will be bringing his passion for storytelling and technical expertise back to Interlochen's 29 film and animation students.

CHRISTOPHER MOREHOUSE, CONDUCTOR OF WIND SYMPHONY

Morehouse joins Interlochen after serving as Director of Bands and Professor of Conducting at Southern Illinois University. In 2008, he made his Carnegie Hall debut with the SIU Wind Ensemble at the New York Band and Orchestra Festival, working with notable composers. Morehouse's artistic collaborations include composers-in-residence Augusta Read Thomas, Morten Lauridsen, Bernard Rands, Chen Yi, Susan Botti, and Dana Wilson, among others. He is also published in ten volumes of the Teaching Music through Performance in Band series published by GIA Publications.

Among the new faculty, adjunct and visiting professors announced are also André Peele (Interim Instructor of Voice), Meredith Stemen (Collaborative Pianist), David Wharton (Instructor of Trumpet), Fez Avery (Visiting Instructor of Creative Writing), Daniel Kohler (Instructor of Math & Science), Kimberly Baker (Instructor of English), Kevin Postma (Instructor of Science), Jennifer Decew (Instructor of Math), Jacob Wheeler (Adjunct Instructor of Journalism), Jill Beauchamp (Adjunct Instructor of English).

About Interlochen Center for the Arts

The nonprofit Interlochen Center for the Arts is a recipient of the National Medal of Arts and the only organization in the world that brings together a 3,000-student summer camp program; a 550-plus-student fine arts boarding high school; a year-round source of expert online arts education for children, teens, and adults; opportunities for adults to engage in fulfilling artistic and creative programs; two 24-hour, listener-supported public radio services (classical music and news); more than 600 arts presentations annually by students, faculty, and world-renowned guest artists; a robust hospitality division that curates on-campus lodging, dining, and transportation services; and a global alumni base spanning nine decades, including leaders in the arts and all other endeavors. For information, visit Interlochen online at www.interlochen.org.

TOKYO, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- PubMatic (Nasdaq: PUBM), the leading AI-powered ad tech company delivering digital advertising performance, today announced that Nippon Television Network Corporation ("Nippon TV"), Japan's leading broadcaster, has named PubMatic as the primary international partner for Sugree, its programmatic TV advertising platform.

PubMatic will serve as the central point of contact for global advertisers seeking access to Sugree inventory. Through PubMatic's regional teams across North America, EMEA, and APAC, international buyers can now access Nippon TV's broadcast inventory – which, according to internal NTV data, reaches more than 100 million monthly active users through entertainment, news, sports, and drama programming - through a single relationship, with local language support, centralized campaign management, and end-to-end operational coverage from onboarding through billing.

Expanding access to Japanese broadcast television

Japan is the world's fourth-largest advertising market, and television remains its highest-reach, most trusted media channel — yet for international advertisers, accessing premium Japanese terrestrial broadcast inventory has historically been complex. Language barriers, time zone differences, and market-specific operational requirements have made direct engagement with Japanese broadcasters difficult to navigate at scale. This partnership directly addresses that friction.

Mr. Naohiko Arai, Director and Managing Executive Officer of Nippon TV, said: "Since partnering with PubMatic as Sugree's Premier Partner, we have highly valued the important role they have played in bridging the gap between international advertisers and the Japanese broadcast advertising market. Their global footprint, combined with a deep understanding of both programmatic advertising and our local market requirements, makes them an invaluable partner in helping us scale internationally. As international interest in Sugree continues to grow, we look forward to working with PubMatic as our trusted partner for international business to expand global demand and create new business opportunities. Together, we will connect advertisers around the world with Nippon TV's audiences and bring the value of Japanese terrestrial television advertising to a broader global market."

Building on a record of performance

Since being named Premier Partner for Sugree in 2025, PubMatic has worked closely with Nippon TV to expand programmatic access to Japan's premium terrestrial broadcast inventory. That work was recognized with Nippon TV's Ad Reach Max Award for FY2025, a performance-based recognition reflecting PubMatic's contribution to audience reach and advertiser outcomes on the platform.

Ken Aihara, Country Manager Japan at PubMatic, said: "International advertisers have told us that Japan is a market they want to be in, but haven't known how to enter efficiently. What this partnership does is remove that barrier. When a global buyer wants to access Nippon TV inventory through Sugree, they come to us. We handle the relationship, the setup, the reporting, and the ongoing management — in their language, in their time zone. Japan's premium broadcast inventory is now as accessible as inventory in any other market we operate in."

Launched in 2025, Sugree is Japan's first programmatic TV advertising platform enabling impression-based transactions for television advertising. This expanded partnership aims to accelerate adoption of Japanese premium broadcast inventory among global advertisers while supporting Sugree's international growth.

International brands and agencies interested in Sugree inventory should contact their PubMatic account representative or visit PubMatic.com.

PubMatic (NASDAQ: PUBM) is the leading AI-powered ad tech company delivering digital advertising performance. Through an intelligent, unified platform that connects buyers, publishers, data partners, and commerce media networks, PubMatic delivers superior performance with greater transparency, control, and efficiency.

Since 2006, PubMatic has pioneered every major advance in programmatic advertising, from enabling the first OpenRTB transactions to embedding AI-driven optimization and privacy-focused innovation across its platform. With omnichannel scale, proven reliability, and a track record of continuous innovation, PubMatic is building a more intelligent, profitable, and sustainable digital advertising ecosystem. Built to Connect. Powered to Perform.

Nippon Television Network Corporation (Nippon TV) is Japan's first commercial broadcaster, having launched in 1953. Today, it is a leading multiplatform media company engaged in a wide range of media businesses beyond traditional broadcasting, including the production and distribution of television programs and video content, streaming services, film, live events, international operations, and licensing. With a strong foundation built on creative excellence and trusted broadcast quality, Nippon TV combines its content creation capabilities, technological expertise, and drive for innovation to deliver new value that goes beyond terrestrial broadcasting. By working closely with domestic and international partners, Nippon TV is committed to shaping the future of media and contributing to a sustainable and enriched information society.

LOS ANGELES, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ACME Media, the parent of ACME AI, and David Ayer today announced that Ayer has joined ACME Media as a Partner and Principal. The deal also includes an overall production partnership between ACME and Ayer.

Ayer most recently released HEART OF THE BEAST, which was met with audience and critical acclaim, earning almost $200M at the global box office.

The addition of Ayer will strengthen the continued development of the studio's production system to make ACME Media the most filmmaker-friendly ecosystem in the industry: increasing its production slate, developing production capabilities and elevating its own production pipeline.

The partnership comes at a moment when the industry is facing a decline in film production, shrinking budgets and much uncertainty. ACME is helping reshape the landscape as it delivers full photo real 16-bit 4K output, while simultaneously lowering budgets and bringing back the mid-budget film model. ACME has six original films underway, along with more than ten projects from third-party studios and production companies at various stages of development, including BITCOIN, which is currently in post-production.

ACME pioneered "the grey box" (trademarked) and its proprietary performance capture methodology which leads to a 50-75% reduction in production time and cost which gives each film and filmmaker more flexibility, tools and coverage. Part of ACME's unique product and process is its filmmaker-centric approach. With the help of Ayer, ACME has built and mapped virtually every lens and every lighting package a filmmaker relies on, so the worlds that surround the performance are 100% photoreal.

"David is the most technical and specific director I have ever met," said Kavanaugh. "His knowledge of the chemistry, physics, lighting and overall details of filmmaking is unparalleled, which makes him the perfect person to help us build and evolve our systems. His love of movies, his love of the process and his passion to preserve filmmaking makes this partnership especially exciting. We share the joint vision that the art of filmmaking is at the heart of everything we do. Thanks to his help our systems are more fine-tuned and specific, made for the most discerning directors with every tool they could want now available."

"I joined ACME because our business is in need of serious help," said Ayer. "Original movies are not getting made due to budget issues and uncertainty of this business. This is at the heart of ACME -- thanks to our technology a film can be made in less time and less budget without sacrificing the creative vision or the jobs. At ACME the performance is photographed exactly as it is on a typical production: the same camera, the same crew, the same process. The actor's performance is not touched. The director still owns the frame. The crew still does the work. That is the heart of ACME. Ryan has been at the center of many of the biggest changes this business has made in twenty years," said Ayer. "He knows what a director needs and what a studio can afford, and he built ACME for both."

Together, Ayer and Kavanaugh see ACME as more than the next step for the film business. It is a way for the business to find its footing again, with original ideas made at a cost that works. It is also a step back into the days of true artistic expression, with the tools to match. 

ABOUT ACME MEDIA:

ACME Media is a film and television studio and the parent company of ACME AI, the most prolific studio working in AI today. ACME's principals have produced, financed or distributed more than 250 films with more than $17 billion in global box office. They created slate co-financing, built the structure that allowed Marvel to make its own films, co-created the subscription streaming window with Netflix and built the largest mini-major studio of its era. Their films have received over 60 Academy Award® nominations. Based in Los Angeles and London with AI artists worldwide, ACME pioneered the Grey Box studio and completed the first all performance capture AI film BITCOIN, currently in post-production. The film is directed by Doug Liman and stars Casey Affleck, Gal Gadot, Pete Davidson and Isla Fisher. ACME has more than twelve films in various stages of production.

SANTA MONICA, Calif., Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Universal Music Group (UMG), the world leader in music-based entertainment, today announced the appointment of Ignacio Meyer as President of Universal Music Latin America & Iberian Peninsula, effective immediately. Meyer will report to Felipe Holguin, who was named CEO of the division yesterday.

Meyer will bring his wide-ranging experience in creative strategy and artist development, along with his relationships throughout the creative community, to UMG's operations across Latin America and Iberia. Working with Holguin and UMG's local and global teams, he will draw on their complementary expertise and shared spirit of innovation to find new ways to support artists and connect their music with audiences around the world.

Holguin said: "Artists are at the heart of how we're building this next chapter. Nacho combines creative sensibility and strategic vision with a deep understanding of how to nurture each artist's individuality, grow their audience, and heighten their impact across platforms. He'll add a powerful dimension to our leadership team as we invest in extraordinary artists and bring bold ideas to life. We know from experience how well we work together, and I'm delighted to welcome him to UMG."

Meyer said: "Latin music is shaping culture around the world because its artists keep pushing boundaries by embracing new sounds, new technologies, and new ways to connect with fans. Their creative ambition is a force for the entire industry. Our role is to amplify that vision with the right support, fresh thinking, and UMG's global reach. I'm excited to work with Felipe and our teams to help artists build lasting careers and take their music even further."

Meyer has held leadership roles at TelevisaUnivision since 2011, spanning US networks and local media, radio, music and non-scripted entertainment, business development, and strategic partnerships. Most recently, as President, U.S. Networks & Local Media, he led the business as Univision reclaimed its position as the No. 1 Spanish-language network in the United States and delivered the highest rated music award shows in the US amongst Hispanic audiences.

As Executive Vice President, Music & Non-Scripted Entertainment, Meyer oversaw Univision's music business, cross-platform programming strategy and major live events, including the executive production of award-winning shows such as Premio Lo Nuestro, Premios Juventud, and the Latin GRAMMY Awards. His responsibilities also included artist-development efforts in the U.S. and globally, as well as strategic business development initiatives across music, music publishing, and sound design. He also led franchise development and corporate partnerships, direct-to-consumer initiatives, experiential marketing, and licensing. During his Univision tenure, Uforia launched U-LAB, a program that paired emerging artists with artistic mentorship and digital distribution.

Before joining Univision, Meyer founded and served as Managing Partner of strategic advisory firm Konexxion Enterprises. Earlier in his career, he began working with artists directly as a manager, served on the management team of IFPI Latin America (an industry body representing 1500+ recorded music companies), and helped establish The Latin Recording Academy as an independent organization dedicated to advancing Latin music and its creators around the world.

NEW YORK, Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- NowThis, the social-first media brand built for Gen Z female audiences with original shortform franchises, creator-led formats and issue-aware storytelling across major social platforms, today announced it has acquired Impact Media (Impact Digital Group), the award-winning media company behind @impact and @environment. Terms of the deal were not disclosed.

The acquisition grows NowThis' audience and deepens its investment in franchise-driven social video for younger, highly engaged communities. Several members of the Impact Media team will join NowThis as part of the deal.

The deal also sharpens NowThis' approach to political and impact-driven content. @impact will remain a separate channel from NowThis Impact, serving a complementary audience. While NowThis Impact delivers deeper political and policy coverage, @impact connects socially conscious audiences with the issues shaping their everyday lives through a culture-first lens. Together, the two channels give NowThis two distinct entry points into politically engaged, progressive-minded audiences.

The move deepens NowThis' shift toward franchise-driven, audience-owned content rather than one-off viral moments. Impact Media's properties reach more than 4 million followers across platforms and over 55 million unique viewers monthly, adding a highly engaged, culture-forward audience that complements NowThis' existing Gen Z female audience of socially native viewers. The acquisition broadens NowThis' overall footprint.

"This acquisition is about finding audiences who are already showing up, and giving them more of what keeps them coming back," said Sharon Mussalli, CEO of NowThis. "Impact Media's team and community bring exactly the kind of engagement we're building around - durable, repeatable franchises that live beyond any single platform or post."

"Impact helps young audiences make sense of the issues shaping their lives," said Michael Vito Valentino, Editor-in-Chief of NowThis. "We're bringing NowThis's video expertise to that work, giving its community new ways to engage with the stories that matter to them."

"We built Impact on the belief that social-first media for Gen Z could be a lasting business," said Tim Chau, Co-Founder, Impact Media. "This acquisition marks a new chapter for what we started, with the opportunity to grow the community and connection at its heart."

"Understanding what matters to our audience has always guided Impact's work," said Michelle Andrews, Co-Founder, Impact Media. "We're excited to see Impact evolve with NowThis and the opportunities ahead for the brand."

NowThis is redefining media for a new generation. A digital-first brand reaching more than 100 million people globally each month, NowThis is GenZTV - built for a Gen Z female audience across every channel we run. We're transforming scrolling into tuning in, turning bingeable, social-first content into destination viewing on the platforms where our audience already lives.

releases.body:
Experienced media & music executive and entrepreneur to lead UMG's Latin operations, building on the region's global momentum and deepening the company's commitment to artists

 

SANTA MONICA, Calif., Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Universal Music Group (UMG), the world leader in music-based entertainment, today announced the appointment of Felipe Holguin as CEO of Universal Music Latin America & Iberian Peninsula, effective immediately. He will report to Sir Lucian Grainge, Chairman and CEO of UMG.

A versatile executive and entrepreneur with more than thirty years of experience across music, media, technology, and finance in the U.S., Latin America, and Europe, Holguin has built creative businesses, led digital organizations, and helped drive strategy and M&A across the region.

Holguin will lead UMG's Latin music operations across the U.S., Latin America, and Iberia. Working with the company's local and global teams, he will help identify and develop the next generation of talent, support artists at every stage of their careers, amplify the region's diverse music and cultures, and bring UMG's deep catalog to new generations of listeners around the world.

The appointment follows Jesús López's decision to take on a new role as Chairman Emeritus of Global Talent Services, the artist management and services company he conceived. UMG and its artists will continue to benefit from his wide-ranging expertise, relationships, and insight into the business.

Sir Lucian Grainge, Chairman and CEO of UMG, said: "Latin music has led the way in opening global audiences to artists around the world, showing how music can cross borders while staying rooted in the cultures that give it life. Its many voices and sounds continue to expand what's possible and point toward what's next. Felipe combines deep respect for artistry and the Latin creative ecosystem with expertise across business, technology, and data. I'm excited to see him work with our teams to invest in the extraordinary and the unexpected and to create more global opportunities for artists."

Holguin said: "Artists are the ultimate change agents. Our role is to bring together the ideas, platforms, and partnerships that help them reach fans and move culture forward. Jesús and the talented people across Latin America and Iberia have helped shape Latin music's global rise. I'm excited to work with UMG's teams across the globe to build our company around artists and help their music travel even further."

Jesús López said: "I'm proud to welcome Felipe to UMG. He's an accomplished leader with a clear vision for the future, and I'm confident he'll build on the extraordinary foundation our teams have created. I look forward to supporting the company as we continue our shared mission of helping artists realize the full scope of their ambitions."

At Univision Communications, Holguin served as CEO of Fusion Media Group, where he transformed operations, integrated digital acquisitions, and grew the company's English-language division to 92 million monthly unique visitors, at the time the largest digital publisher in its competitive set. He also served as Executive Vice President of Digital, News and Music at Univision, leading strategy, operations, and M&A across Univision.com, including its music streaming and audio platform and televised music award-show franchises. Earlier in his career, Holguin co-founded Page One Media, publisher of PODER, a business magazine for Hispanic leaders in the U.S., Mexico, Colombia, Peru, and Chile. The company was sold to Televisa.

Most recently, Holguin worked with HYBE Latin America on strategy and operations. He previously worked with Exile Content Studio on the launch, growth, and sale of its music business to HYBE, as well as on the company's strategy and development, including its acquisition by Candle Media.

Holguin holds an MBA from Harvard Business School and dual engineering degrees from Worcester Polytechnic Institute.

releases.title: Brandon Lesando of Beachside High School Named Recipient of the 2026 George N. Parks Award from the National Association for Music Education and Music for All
releases.body:
HERNDON, Va., Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The National Association for Music Education (NAfME) is pleased to honor Brandon Lesando, Director of Bands at Beachside High School, St. Augustine, Florida, as the recipient of the 2026 George N. Parks Award for Leadership in Music Education. Lesando was presented the award during the Music for All and Bands of America Grand National Championships Finals Opening Ceremony in Indianapolis, Indiana, on November 14, 2026.

The George N. Parks Award honors an exemplary music educator who embodies the characteristics and leadership that Mr. Parks showed his students every day. The recipient must have a collaborative spirit, dedication to knowing the students as people, perseverance and enthusiasm, and an ability to instill qualities in students beyond musical achievement.

"NAfME celebrates the contributions of Brandon Lesando to the music education profession and the impact he has had on so many music students," stated NAfME President Cecil Adderley. "We are pleased to join Music for All in honoring him as the 2026 recipient of the George N. Parks Award for Leadership in Music Education. His engaging and inclusive approach to teaching music to students of all ages and abilities will doubtless have lifelong positive repercussions in their lives, and the value of that impression cannot be understated."

Addressing how he nurtures a classroom culture of community and service, Lesando shares, "I hope students leave our program understanding that leadership does not require a title, and service does not require recognition. Both begin with recognizing that what we do, and what we choose not to do, affects the people around us."

Brandon Lesando has spent more than a decade in band education. Prior to his current position launching a newer program at Beachside High School in St. Augustine, Florida, he spent more than nine years at Blue Valley Southwest High School in Overland Park, Kansas, as Assistant Director of Bands for a year before becoming Director of Bands. Prior to that, he "served in the U.S. Navy for 7.5 years as a nuclear submariner in order to finance his undergraduate degree and earned many accolades along the way," shared colleague Dr. Laura K. Bock, Assistant Professor of Music Education and Coordinator of Music Education at San José State University. "After being honorably discharged, he began school at the University of North Florida and completed his teaching certification, working part-time as a band director during the last two years of his degree."

"I have known Brandon for more than 20 years," shared Dr. Edward F. Protzman, Director of Bands and Assistant Professor of Music Education at Portland State University, "first as his teacher and later as a colleague, and I can think of few music educators who better represent the qualities of perseverance, leadership, service, and commitment to students that this award seeks to recognize." Protzman is also the 2019 recipient of the George Parks Award. "Nothing about his journey into the profession was handed to him. He earned it through persistence, sacrifice, discipline, and an unwavering belief that education and hard work could change the course of his life," continued Protzman in his description of Lesando's challenging life as a student and determination to become a music educator.

"During my time working with Brandon," added Bock, "I saw countless examples of the ways he consistently showed up for students and put them first. In addition to the positive experiences that he creates through music instruction, Brandon takes the time to get to know students on an individual basis, celebrate their strengths, and help every student learn and grow. Brandon and I worked together to develop a class that integrated students with severe and multiple disabilities in our percussion class and were recognized by our colleagues for those inclusive efforts."

Lesando shares a story about a student who had a significant influence on his personal value of inclusivity, "Zack, a special education student who came to our program with significant exceptionalities. . . . we found a place for him in our front ensemble and taught him to play suspended cymbal, auxiliary percussion, toms, and—his favorite—the slapstick. His parts were not there simply so he could participate. They contributed musically to our marching shows and concerts, and we held him to that expectation. With support from his paraprofessional and our staff, Zack eventually learned to count and keep time independently. He was not just included in the band. He was a member of the band, relied upon by the people around him, and his excitement when he got a part right was infectious."

"Zack made me a better teacher," continued Lesando, "because he challenged assumptions about what a student was capable of and reinforced something I now believe deeply: Success is not about everyone reaching the same destination. It is creating an environment where every student is expected to grow, contribute, and understand that their contribution matters to the people around them."

"When I revisited my copy of The Dynamic Drum Major and pulled up the list of characteristics that Mr. Parks believed are embodied by a great leader, they are 'Confidence, Pride, Intensity, Authority, Enthusiasm, Energy, Determination, Self-Discipline, and Dignity'," shared Bock. "Anyone who knows Brandon know that it's hard to miss these qualities and that they're all apparent within minutes of meeting him or watching him teach."

"His students see in him an example of what can be accomplished through perseverance, personal responsibility, and determination," shared Protzman. "He understands that students arrive in our classrooms carrying circumstances we may know nothing about, and he has an extraordinary ability to see potential in young people and challenge them to become more than they may believe is possible. . . . For me, Brandon's career represents one of the most meaningful outcomes we can hope for as educators."

Developed by NAfME and Music for All, the award is named for George N. Parks (1953–2010), director of the University of Massachusetts Minuteman Marching Band at the University of Massachusetts Amherst from 1977 until his death. Considered a national authority on drum majoring, he led the George N. Parks Drum Major Academy®, a summer workshop program for high school drum majors. View past recipients here.

The National Association for Music Education (NAfME) is a collaborative community that supports music educators and advocates for equitable access to music education. The only association that addresses all aspects of music education, NAfME, together with its affiliated state music education associations, advocates at the national, state, and local levels and provides resources and opportunities for teachers, students, parents, and administrators. Founded in 1907 and representing more than 57,000 members teaching millions of students, NAfME advances the music education profession and promotes lifelong experiences in music. 

Follow NAfME on Instagram and Facebook @NAfME. For additional information, contact Catherina Hurlburt at catherinah@nafme.org or 571-323-3395.

releases.body:
BlackRock's Nick Nefouse Discusses Guaranteed Income, the Evolution of 401(k)s, and the Future of Retirement Security

WASHINGTON, Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The National Institute on Retirement Security (NIRS) today released Episode 7 of its Retirement in America podcast, "Making the 401(k) Look More Like a Pension: The Future of Lifetime Retirement Income."

The episode features Nick Nefouse, Global Head of Retirement Solutions and Head of LifePath at BlackRock, joining podcast host and NIRS Executive Director Dan Doonan to discuss how retirement plans are evolving to help Americans turn their savings into reliable income throughout retirement.

Retirement in America is available on the NIRS website, YouTube and all major podcast platforms.

For decades, traditional pensions provided workers with predictable monthly income for life. But as private-sector employers have shifted toward 401(k) plans, workers increasingly bear responsibility not only for saving and investing, but also for determining how to make their savings last throughout retirement. The podcast conversation explores how innovations in retirement plan design could bring some of the most valuable features of traditional pensions into today's 401(k) system.

"Saving enough for retirement is only part of the challenge. Americans also need help turning those savings into income they can count on for the rest of their lives," Doonan said. "Nick offers an interesting perspective on how the retirement industry is rethinking 401(k) plans to address that challenge. As more Americans retire without traditional pensions, addressing this gap will reduce financial-related stress in retirement by adding back some of the certainty that so many workers have lost in recent decades."

A central focus of the discussion is BlackRock's LifePath Paycheck®, a retirement investment solution that integrates access to a guaranteed lifetime income stream provided by third-party insurers into a target-date strategy. As participants approach retirement, the strategy gradually builds an allocation to group annuity contracts, which participants may elect to convert into a lifetime income stream while keeping the remainder of their savings invested and accessible. Nefouse explains how this approach seeks to provide greater income certainty in retirement while reducing the need for workers to make complex investment and income-planning decisions on their own.

Among the topics discussed in the episode:

  • Making 401(k)s work more like pensions. How retirement plans are evolving beyond accumulating savings to help workers generate dependable income throughout retirement, incorporating professional investment management and features traditionally associated with pensions.
  • The challenge of spending retirement savings. Why retirees often hesitate to draw down their savings, even when they have accumulated substantial assets, and how predictable income can help them make more confident spending decisions.
  • The role of employers and retirement plan design. How workplace plans can offer institutional investment management, fiduciary oversight and potentially lower costs, along with the challenges employers face in adopting new retirement income solutions.
  • The future of retirement investing. The potential role of private-market investments, participant education and public policy in helping retirement plans deliver better long-term outcomes.
  • BlackRock's LifePath Paycheck strategy. How the strategy integrates access to guaranteed lifetime income into a target-date strategy, with the ability to convert a portion of the portfolio into a lifetime income stream, providing a paycheck for life in retirement, while keeping remaining assets invested and accessible.

Retirement in America is a NIRS podcast exploring the economic, workforce and policy issues shaping Americans' retirement security.

The National Institute on Retirement Security is a nonprofit, nonpartisan organization established to contribute to informed policymaking by fostering a deep understanding of the value of retirement security to employees, employers, and the economy as a whole. Located in Washington, D.C., NIRS membership includes financial services firms, employee benefit plans, trade associations, and other retirement service providers.

Founder David Plotz hands leadership to longtime business partner as City Cast, with 1.5 million listeners and readers across 13 cities, reimagines local media for how people live now

WASHINGTON, Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- City Cast, the local media network connecting people to the cities they love, has named co-founder Andi McDaniel as chief executive officer. McDaniel succeeds founder David Plotz, who is departing after six years of building City Cast from a two-person startup into a 13-city network reaching 1.5 million people. McDaniel will guide City Cast's next phase: expanding audiences, accelerating revenue growth, and embracing new platforms.

Plotz and McDaniel founded City Cast in 2020 on a simple belief: people are more connected than ever, and somehow less connected to the places they live. As local newspapers, community institutions, and shared rituals have faded, City Cast set out to become the new thread — a daily conversation about what's happening in your city, and why it matters. City Cast has expanded from daily audio podcasts and newsletters into a fully multiplatform local media company, with video on Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube, live events, and Neighbors, City Cast's paid membership program. City Cast has also recently established a 16-person local newsroom for its Washington, DC outlet.

"Building City Cast has been the proudest achievement of my career," Plotz said. "We've created something from nothing, growing from two employees to 122 and building a company that's ambitious and experimental, with a culture that's joyful and kind. Andi has been central to that work from the beginning, and she's exactly the visionary leader City Cast needs for what comes next."

At a time when local newspapers are shrinking and media companies are cutting staff, City Cast is one of the few local networks growing across multiple cities. The company recently posted its strongest revenue quarter. Most of City Cast's audience is between 21 and 44 — a cohort traditional local media has struggled to reach.

"People care as much as ever about what's happening where they live. They just want it delivered in a way that fits their lives," said McDaniel. "City Cast is showing that it's possible to reach younger audiences with local news and information they care about and are willing to pay for."

McDaniel has shaped City Cast's editorial voice, talent and brand since its launch, first as chief creative officer and recently as interim CEO. Before City Cast, McDaniel was chief content officer at WAMU, NPR's Washington station, where she led the development of the national daily program 1A, launched a podcast division and oversaw a period in which the station's audience grew larger, younger and more diverse and its revenue nearly doubled.

"City Cast is building something new in local media, reaching younger audiences on the platforms where they spend the most time," said Tim O'Shaughnessy, President and Chief Executive Officer of Graham Holdings Company, City Cast's parent company. "I am thrilled that Andi McDaniel will lead City Cast in its next chapter, where we aim to turn our extensive local reach into an excellent business. Andi's ability to understand what local communities want, her extensive background leading editorial organizations, and her drive to build new business models give her the perfect trifecta to be the next CEO of City Cast."

About City Cast

City Cast is a network of local media outlets making podcasts, newsletters, and social content in 13 U.S. cities.Through daily conversations, local news, and recommendations for making the most of city life, City Cast helps residents stay informed, curious and connected. City Cast operates in 13 cities: Austin, Chicago, Denver, Las Vegas, Madison, Nashville, Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, Portland, Salt Lake City, Seattle, the Twin Cities and Washington, D.C. City Cast is part of Graham Holdings Company. Learn more at citycast.fm.

releases.title: Creative Currency Acquires Launch Media
releases.body:
TORONTO and ST. JOHN'S, NL, Nov. 2, 2026 /CNW/ -- Creative Currency, the Toronto-based advertising agency and content studio, today announced it has acquired Launch Media, a fast-growing Newfoundland and Labrador marketing agency. As part of the firm's first new acquisition, Creative Currency named St. John's its Atlantic Canada headquarters.

Launch Media founder and President Chris Dunne joins Creative Currency as Vice President, Atlantic Canada. He will lead the firm's growth across Newfoundland and Labrador, Nova Scotia, New Brunswick and Prince Edward Island, with a mandate to expand and scale clients, talent and revenue in the region.

The acquisition supercharges Creative Currency's existing Halifax team as the agency now has two Atlantic Canada offices and a deeper bench on the ground, giving clients across all four provinces more capacity, faster turnaround and local insight.

"Atlantic Canada is key growth market for us and we have always known that to win in this market you need to show up, in person and on the ground," said Dennis Matthews, President of Creative Currency. "Chris is a builder who knows what it takes to win in Newfoundland and Labrador and across the region. He took Launch from one client to a roster with national reach in three years. That's the ambition we look for, and we're proud to have him and his team on board."

A growth story on both sides of the deal

Launch Media opened in 2023 with a single client. In three years it has built a team of 10 designers, content creators, digital marketers and strategists, with clients in automotive, ocean technology, logistics, financial services and food, and a growing national footprint. That growth brought Launch to an inflection point. The next stage demands scale: deeper creative and production capacity, national media buying, and the backing to compete for larger mandates. Joining Creative Currency delivers all three.

For Creative Currency, ranked No. 1 on Adweek's 2024 Fastest Growing Agencies list, the transaction adds an established book of business, a proven team and a permanent footprint on the ground in one of Canada's most dynamic regional markets. Launch Media clients gain Creative Currency's national creative, content and public affairs capabilities.

"We built Launch to punch above our weight. Now we don't have to," said Chris Dunne, Vice President, Atlantic Canada. "Our clients keep the people they know and gain the firepower of a national agency. Our team gets a bigger stage without leaving home. St. John's just became an Atlantic headquarters, and we intend to earn it."

An extended offering from Enterprise Canada

Creative Currency's sister agency, Enterprise Canada, also benefits from this transaction by gaining client relationships and increased capacity on the ground. For more about Enterprise Canada, a leading national strategic communications firm: https://enterprisecanada.com

"We are proud to welcome Chris and the Launch team to our broader full-service offering," said David Tarrant, Vice President, National Strategic Communications and Practice Lead, Atlantic Canada at Enterprise Canada and Strategic Advisor, Creative Currency. "Since Enterprise Canada opened our initial office in Halifax in 2021, our Atlantic Canadian team has grown by combining the very best talent in the entire country with a deep understanding of the local marketplace, delivering a unique offering. Creative Currency opening a new headquarters in my home province of Newfoundland and Labrador is an exciting next step in this journey."

What the deal means

  • Headquarters: St. John's becomes Creative Currency's Atlantic Canada HQ, informally known as CC Atlantic, alongside Halifax to drive growth across all four provinces.
  • Leadership: Chris Dunne is appointed Vice President, Atlantic Canada, reporting to President Dennis Matthews.
  • Team: Launch Media's full team joins Creative Currency.
  • Clients: Launch Media clients keep the team they know, now backed by a national agency.
  • Strategy: This is the first step in a disciplined growth plan. Creative Currency will keep evaluating opportunities to add talent, capabilities and markets across Canada.

About Creative Currency

Creative Currency is a Toronto-based, full-service advertising agency and content studio working at the intersection of advertising and public affairs. Spun out of Enterprise Canada in 2021, the agency brings together creative thinking, strategic communications and a deep understanding of public policy to help brands, organizations and causes tell compelling stories, shape public opinion and inspire action. It was ranked No. 1 on Adweek's 2024 Fastest Growing Agencies list. Creative Currency has offices across Canada, in St. John's, Halifax, Ottawa, Toronto, Hamilton, Calgary and Vancouver. Learn more at creativecurrency.ca.

About Launch Media

Founded in St. John's in 2023, Launch Media Inc. is a Newfoundland and Labrador marketing agency serving clients in automotive, ocean technology, logistics, financial services and food. Launch is now part of Creative Currency.

About Enterprise Canada

Enterprise Canada is a leading national strategic communications firm and Creative Currency's sister agency. Learn more at enterprisecanada.com.

NEW YORK, Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Better Business Advice has named CapCut a top choice in a 2026 review of AI software for social media marketing, highlighting support for campaign planning, advertising concepts, and post-launch creative revisions. The review examines how businesses can use AI-assisted tools to develop promotional materials around marketing objectives rather than simply produce more social media content.

The recognition addresses a practical challenge for small businesses and lean marketing teams. A single promotion may require multiple advertising angles, visual formats, approvals, and adjustments after launch. CapCut supports several stages of that process through three creative tools.

Best AI Software for Social Media Marketing:

  • Seedream - CapCut's AI image generator that turns written marketing briefs into visual concepts, mood boards, and promotional image drafts.
  • Seedance 2.0 - CapCut's AI video generator that creates motion-based drafts for advertising hooks, product demonstrations, launch teasers, and campaign storyboards.
  • AI Image Extender - CapCut's image editing tool that expands backgrounds to help adapt campaign visuals for different layouts and advertising placements.

Why CapCut Is a Practical Choice for Social Media Marketing

Social media campaigns begin with a business objective, whether generating leads, increasing store visits, or driving online sales. Effective creative assets need to communicate a relevant benefit, present a clear offer, and support the intended action.

Better Business Advice recognizes CapCut for helping translate those priorities into visual materials. Seedream supports early direction, Seedance 2.0 supports promotional video concepts, and AI Image Extender supports subsequent adaptations. The combined workflow is particularly relevant when production resources are limited, or campaigns require frequent updates.

The advantage is flexibility across campaign stages, not automatic marketing decisions. Businesses still determine audience targeting, offers, budgets, and performance goals.

How Seedream Helps Turn Marketing Briefs Into Visual Campaign Concepts

A product can support several promotional messages. A travel mug, for example, might be positioned around everyday commuting, outdoor activities, or temperature retention. Each approach calls for a different visual treatment.

Seedream converts prompts into concept images that can be compared before a photo shoot or final design is commissioned. Better Business Advice identifies three elements that make those prompts more useful:

  • Audience and objective: Define the customer and desired response.
  • Offer and message: Specify the benefit, promotion, or customer problem.
  • Creative direction: Establish setting, tone, branding requirements, and format.

This structure helps reviewers judge visual drafts against the campaign brief rather than personal preference alone. Generated imagery still requires checks for product accuracy, brand consistency, and realistic advertising claims before publication.

How Seedance 2.0 Supports Testing Different Social Media Ad Messages

Video advertising often depends on the opening message. A demonstration highlighting a product feature may appeal to a different audience than a lifestyle-led promotion of the same item.

Seedance 2.0 can turn alternative written concepts into motion drafts for storyboards, launch teasers, and product demonstrations. That capability makes exploring distinct advertising hooks more practical before committing to full production.

The Better Business Advice review also connects creative variations with A/B testing. A controlled comparison might change the opening scene while keeping the audience, offer, and landing page consistent. Marketers can then assess whether the creative difference affects the intended result.

CapCut creates visual materials; advertising platforms supply performance data. Relevant measures include click-through rate for traffic campaigns, qualified leads for inquiry campaigns, and cost per purchase for online sales. High view counts alone do not establish advertising effectiveness.

How AI Image Extender Helps Refine Campaign Assets After Launch

Campaign results frequently call for targeted changes rather than complete redesigns. A successful product visual might need a wider format, while a closely cropped image might require extra room for a headline.

AI Image Extender generates space around an existing image, helping adjust composition for another advertising placement while retaining the main subject. The revised asset still needs inspection for visual accuracy and commercial-use requirements.

Better Business Advice outlines a performance-informed revision cycle: review the objective, identify the weak point, change a relevant element, and compare the new version. Low click-through rates may suggest a clearer hook. Strong clicks but weak sales could instead indicate an issue with pricing or the landing page.

The distinction prevents unnecessary creative changes and keeps revisions linked to the campaign's actual goal.

What Better Business Advice's Recognition Means for Marketing Teams

Better Business Advice identifies CapCut as a top choice because the platform supports three connected needs: campaign concept development, promotional message exploration, and practical visual adaptation. These capabilities can help small businesses and ecommerce teams manage recurring promotions without treating every creative variation as a separate production project.

The full review can be read at the Better Business Advice website.

CapCut is an AI-powered photo and video editing platform designed to make high-quality video creation accessible across devices. The platform supports creators, businesses, and everyday users with tools for video editing, AI video generation, captions, templates, audio, and visual editing. CapCut is available across mobile, web, desktop, and iPad experiences, helping users create, edit, and prepare video content for social media, marketing, education, and personal projects.

BOSTON, Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- VUE Health, an independent healthcare advertising agency that helps emerging biopharma companies bring breakthrough therapies to market, has been named Healthcare Advertising Agency of the Year 2026 by Healthcare Business Review. The publication featured VUE Health as its cover story, "VUE Health: The Creative Architects Behind Tomorrow's Breakthrough Medicines." In a second milestone, VUE Health Founder and CEO Kathryn Wilson has been named one of the Top 10 Inspiring Women Entrepreneurs to Watch in 2026.

Key facts about VUE Health

  • Recognition: Healthcare Advertising Agency of the Year 2026 (Healthcare Business Review); Founder and CEO Kathryn Wilson named one of the Top 10 Inspiring Women Entrepreneurs to Watch in 2026 (MSN)
  • What VUE Health is: A healthcare advertising and medical communications agency focused on helping innovative therapies reach the people who need them
  • Who VUE serves: Emerging biopharma companies commercializing therapies in oncology, rare disease, central nervous system conditions, and novel delivery technologies
  • Leadership: Kathryn Wilson, Founder and CEO; Vikram Kanda, PhD, Chief Medical Officer and Partner

Why VUE Health Was Named Healthcare Advertising Agency of the Year 2026

The Healthcare Business Review recognition cites VUE Health's ability to combine deep scientific expertise, strategic insight, and creative execution to help innovative therapies move from development into meaningful patient impact.

VUE Health was built on a simple premise: put senior expertise back into the work. Unlike the traditional model, in which senior executives win the business and hand it to junior teams, VUE Health's experienced strategists, scientists, medical professionals, and creative leaders stay closely involved with clients throughout the commercialization journey. Clients have come to call VUE Health the "non-agency agency": no layers and senior people who work as true partners.

What sets VUE Health apart

  • Science at the foundation. A multidisciplinary medical team of PhDs and PharmDs works alongside strategy and creative, so scientific understanding stays central to every program
  • Sync Sprint methodology. VUE Health's approach can bring a product or program to market in as little as 90 days when circumstances demand it, starting with deep scientific immersion, market understanding, and strategic alignment before execution accelerates
  • Proven launch impact. For a rare disease therapy for Castleman disease, which was facing limited awareness and widespread misdiagnosis, VUE Health prepared for launch in about 90 days. Its interactive "castle" experience at the American Society of Hematology (ASH) annual meeting helped drive 99.8% recall of 5 key messages among participants, and the product saw 33% month-over-month, year-over-year sales growth
  • AI-enabled, human-led. VUE Health uses technology to enhance human expertise rather than replace it, including internal platforms for workflow and resource management, a proprietary capability that assembles custom teams from employees and a network of vetted experts, and AI tools that make scientific dialogue with key opinion leaders faster and more meaningful
  • Focused on what matters most. VUE Health concentrates on emerging biopharma companies in categories where awareness, diagnosis, and clinical education are often the critical barriers. The agency continues to expand its capabilities across media, public relations, technology platforms, and specialized scientific expertise

Kathryn Wilson: Top 10 Inspiring Women Entrepreneurs to Watch in 2026

Wilson founded VUE Health after rising through senior agency roles and finding herself spending less time solving clients' commercialization challenges and more time managing P&Ls and operations. She built VUE Health to return senior talent to the work itself, and that model now defines the agency's identity. MSN's feature highlights her decades of experience translating complex science into clear, meaningful communication for healthcare professionals and patients and a leadership style grounded in integrity, empathy, and meaningful impact. Her path into the industry began with an early pharmaceutical advertising internship that sparked a lasting passion, and today she is committed to supporting communities and developing future women leaders.

"I built the agency because I wanted to get back to the work that brought me into this industry in the first place, helping companies solve difficult challenges and bringing life-changing and lifesaving medicines to market," said Kathryn Wilson, Founder and CEO of VUE Health.

A Recognition Built by the VUE Health Team

"These honors belong to every person at VUE Health," said Wilson. "Agency of the Year recognizes what our team does every day: our medical team, strategists, creatives, media and account leaders, and the vetted experts who partner with us. My own recognition is really a reflection of the people who chose to build something different with me. We are not trying to become the biggest agency. We are focused on becoming the right partner for companies developing therapies where our experience, expertise, and passion can truly make a difference."

Wilson and VUE Health Chief Medical Officer and Partner Vikram Kanda, PhD, a scientist trained in molecular cardiology, work closely with clients as strategic peers, a model especially valuable for emerging biopharma companies whose first commercial hires are often building a launch with limited internal support.

"Pharmaceutical commercialization depends on scientific accuracy, clinical relevance, and a deep understanding of how healthcare decisions are made," said Dr. Kanda. "Our medical team makes sure the science is never separated from the story. That is what this recognition is about: a team that slows down first to understand the science so our clients can move faster later."

VUE Health also thanks:

  • Vikram Kanda, PhD, Partner and Chief Medical Officer and the medical team for best-in-class medical strategy and education
  • Meaghan Taft, SVP Client Service and the strategy and account teams for ensuring commercial excellence
  • Ohad Cohen, Executive Creative Director and the creative team for hard-hitting and targeted creative and pull-through to impact the attention of the HCP
  • Dan Hurley, SVP Innovation and the omnichannel media team for strategic implementation and execution of omnichannel launch excellence and optimization

About VUE Health

VUE Health is an independent healthcare advertising agency that helps emerging biopharma companies bring breakthrough therapies to market. Named Healthcare Advertising Agency of the Year 2026 by Healthcare Business Review, VUE Health pairs dedicated medical directors on every account with senior strategists and creative leaders who stay hands-on from strategy through launch. Its capabilities span medical strategy, brand and creative, omnichannel media, public relations, market access, and proprietary AI-enabled tools, with deep experience in oncology, rare disease, cardiometabolic, hepatology, and CNS. Learn more at vuehealth.com.

TORONTO, Oct. 26, 2026 /CNW/ -- Canadian pop culture podcast PopTake, hosted by Hugo Filipe and Mikael Melo, has officially joined Stamina Group's media network through a strategic partnership with View the VIBE. The collaboration brings together two entertainment-focused platforms with a shared passion for culture, community and storytelling, with plans to expand PopTake's reach nationally and explore international distribution opportunities.

Now operating as "PopTake, powered by View the VIBE." Your hot takes on music, pop culture and life. The show will benefit from the publication's established Canadian audience, editorial platform and industry/distribution relationships while maintaining the independent voice and creative chemistry that have become its signature.

The partnership also builds on Stamina Group's experience bringing Canadian-produced content to international audiences. Through its globally distributed video podcast Gents Talk, which has secured placement on airline entertainment systems worldwide and through other transportation syndication partners, Stamina Group has established relationships it hopes to leverage to introduce PopTake to audiences beyond Canada.

"Building Stamina Group has always been about amplifying creative voices and connecting audiences through meaningful content," says Steven Branco, Founder & Chief Creative Officer, Stamina Group Inc. and Editor-in-Chief, View the VIBE. "With PopTake's focus on pop culture and View the VIBE's roots in community, culture and entertainment, the partnership felt like a natural fit. Hugo and Mikael have built something special, and we're excited to help take it further. Building on the international success of Gent's Talk and our global distribution partnerships, we see an opportunity to bring PopTake to audiences across Canada and around the world."

Two best friends, plenty of hot takes

Launched in April 2025, PopTake is a weekly entertainment podcast covering music, film, television, celebrity culture and life. Hosted by longtime friends Hugo Filipe and Mikael Melo, the show combines candid commentary, celebrity interviews and social-first content with the energy of a group chat.

Now in its second season, PopTake has built a growing presence on Canada's entertainment circuit, covering major events including TIFF, the JUNO Awards, the Canadian Screen Awards and Osheaga. Its celebrity interviews have featured the likes of Zara Larsson, Katy Perry, Chloe Bailey, JADE, Perrie Edwards, FLO, Sofi Tukker, Patrick J. Adams, Eric McCormack, Lauren Ash, Simple Plan and Holly Humberstone, and more.

The show also features recognizable segments including Backtrack, where artists identify their songs played backwards; This or That, a rapid-fire celebrity interview format where artists must choose between their own songs; and HotTake or FlopTake, featuring the hosts' weekly pop culture verdicts.

"PopTake started as two best friends who couldn't stop talking about pop culture, so we hit record," says Hugo Filipe, Co-Founder & Co-Host, PopTake. "Partnering with View the VIBE puts our takes in front of an audience that loves this stuff, as much as we do."



"We strike the balance between professional and fanboy," adds Mikael Melo, Co-Founder & Co-Host, PopTake . "Our podcast feels like your two internet besties gushing over your favourite artists, and every now and then, we get to interview them. Asking the questions fans actually want answered."

Beyond the podcast, both hosts bring established entertainment and creative industry experience.

Hugo Filipe is a Toronto-based creative director, photographer and entrepreneur. He leads Mister Mister, a creative studio with clients including H&M, RBC, OVO and Campbell's, and owns Nosso Studio, which operates two creative spaces in Toronto.

Mikael Melo is a Canadian Screen Award-winning producer, reporter and digital creator whose credits include ET Canada, Big Brother Canada and The Social. He has interviewed international stars including Katy Perry, Olivia Rodrigo and Florence Pugh, and collaborated with brands including Paramount+, Samsung, Sony Pictures and Universal Music Canada.

What's next for PopTake?

Through the partnership, PopTake will continue producing its weekly podcast and signature social-first content, while exploring expanded editorial collaborations, new sponsors, celebrity interviews, event coverage, branded entertainment opportunities, in-person events and new distribution channels.

The addition of PopTake further strengthens Stamina Group's growing portfolio of International media properties, which includes View the VIBE, WanderEater, Gent's Post and the internationally distributed and acclaimed video podcast, Gent's Talk.

releases.body:
New mural installation by artist A'Darrius Hanible celebrates the country music star as part of the Congress of Country Music's growing public art initiative

PHILADELPHIA, Miss., Oct. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Country music star Lainey Wilson joined GRAMMY Award-winning artist Marty Stuart and community leaders Tuesday for the unveiling of "Wildflowers and Wild Horses," a new mural honoring Wilson in downtown Philadelphia, Mississippi.

"Lainey Wilson is not only a dear friend, but someone who understands the meaning of home," said Marty Stuart. "She knows that no matter how far life takes you or how high your dreams carry you, nothing can replace the people and places that shaped who you are. Lainey came here for this mural unveiling and her fundraiser performances for the Congress of Country Music on nothing more than a hug and a handshake. No contract, no formalities, just friendship, trust and a shared love for where we come from. That tells you everything you need to know about who Lainey Wilson is, and I am so thankful for her support of the Congress of Country Music."

Created by artist A'Darrius Hanible, the mural takes its name and inspiration from Wilson's hit song and celebrates an artist whose distinctive sound, storytelling and authenticity have helped shape a new generation of country music.

The unveiling is part of Marty Stuart's Congress of Country Music's ongoing public art initiative, which brings country music's history and cultural influence to life through murals honoring some of the genre's most recognizable artists.

Wilson attended the ceremony and addressed community members and fans gathered to celebrate the new installation.

"This mural is absolutely beautiful, and I'm so grateful the warm welcome I've received here," said Lainey Wilson. "I brought some of my Mississippi friends along for a little picking and grinning, and that's exactly what I want tonight to be about. A chance to step away from the craziness of everyday life, come together and celebrate the heart of country music. At the end of the day, country music is about storytelling, and there's nothing better than sharing those stories with good people."

The mural was made possible through the support of Aalwese Properties, Hill Real Estate, lafedericks.com, Brent and Annette Federick, and the Riviera Motor Hotel, whose contributions reflect the community's continued investment in downtown Philadelphia's growing arts and cultural landscape.

"Wildflowers and Wild Horses" joins a growing collection of murals throughout downtown Philadelphia honoring influential country music artists and songwriters.
